Like
LAHYK
adj. / adv. / v.
Webster 1828 treats LIKE as adjective (equal; similar / resembling; probable), noun (an equal; a resembling person or thing), adverb (in the same manner; in a manner becoming), and verb (to be pleased with in a moderate degree; to approve — less than love). His own biblical illustrations include James 5:17 (Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are), Revelation 18:18, Daniel 1:19, Matthew 6 / Luke 12 (Solomon not arrayed like one of these), Psalm 103, and 1 Samuel 4:9. This page fills the KJV-gap word of resemblance. Companion pages already treat image, similitude, and idolatry.

Biblical Definition

Like in Scripture is not a brand preference and not a therapy mirror. It names resemblance that either honors God or steals His glory. Jesus will not let prayer copy the heathen: Be not ye therefore like unto them (Matt 6:8). Paul will not let worship shrink God to a mammal: changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man (Rom 1:23). The Son took real flesh: it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren (Heb 2:17). Elijah was not a marble saint: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are (Jas 5:17). John will not let present sonship pretend to be finished glory, and he will not let glory be anything less than Christ: when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is (1 John 3:2). The dictionary therefore keeps like from becoming either idolatry or self-esteem. It is the Bible’s way of saying: resembling this, and not that.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines LIKE as equal or similar; a resembling person or thing; in the same manner; and as a verb, to be pleased with in a moderate degree (less than love). He illustrates from James 5:17, Revelation, Daniel, Matthew 6, Psalm 103, and 1 Samuel 4:9.

expand to see more

LIKE, adjective [Latin , Heb., Gr. See Lick and Lickerish.]

1. Equal in quantity, quality or degree; as a territory of like extent with another; men of like excellence.

2. Similar; resembling; having resemblance.

Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are. James 5:17.

LIKE is usually followed by to or unto, but it is often omitted.

What city is like unto this great city? Revelation 18:18.

I saw three unclean spirits like frogs. Revelation 16:13.

Among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Daniel 1:19.

3. Probably; likely, that is, having the resemblance or appearance of an event; giving reason to expect or believe.

He is like to die of hunger in the place where he is, for there is no more bread. Jeremiah 38:9.

LIKE, noun [elliptically, for like thing, like event, like person.]

1. Some person or thing resembling another; an equal.

LIKE, adverb

1. In the same manner.

Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. Matthew 6:29. Luke 12:27.

LIKE as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. Psalms 103.

2. In a manner becoming.

Be strong, and quit yourselves like men. 1 Samuel 4:9.

LIKE, verb transitive

1. To be pleased with in a moderate degree; to approve. It expresses less than love and delight.

Key Scripture

Matthew 6:8 — "Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him."

Romans 1:23 — "And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things."

Hebrews 2:17 — "Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people."

James 5:17 — "Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months."

1 John 3:2 — "Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is."

Modern Corruption

Like is corrupted when prayer copies the heathen, when God is recast in man’s image, and when we shall be like him is swapped for a mirror that only likes the self.

expand to see more

The first corruption is Matthew 6:8 inverted. Be not ye therefore like unto them forbids pagan prayer-copying. Attractional worship copies the street and calls it relevance. The Father already knows. Likeness to the heathen is not mission; it is disobedience.

The second corruption is Romans 1:23. Glory is changed into an image made like to corruptible man. Process theology and every homemade god shrink the uncorruptible God until He resembles the worshiper. That is idolatry. The recovery is: God is not like us; we are to be made like the Son.

The third corruption is to steal 1 John 3:2. We shall be like him is glorification at His appearing, not a present self-esteem slogan. Therapeutic religion wants a God who is like me now. John points to the appearing. Hebrews 2:17 already told the other half: the Son was made like His brethren in true flesh, not in our sin.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: similar / in the same manner / to be pleased with. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek homoioo (G3666) at Matthew 6:8 and Hebrews 2:17; Greek homoioma (G3667) at Romans 1:23; Greek homoios (G3664) at 1 John 3:2; Greek homoiopathes (G3663) at James 5:17 (tagged on the like passions phrase, not as a separate English like token). No Hebrew number is minted on this page.

expand to see more

Greek homoioo (G3666) — to make like, to be like (Matt 6:8; Heb 2:17).

Greek homoioma (G3667) — likeness, image (Rom 1:23, made like to corruptible man).

Greek homoios (G3664) — like, resembling (1 John 3:2, we shall be like him).

Greek homoiopathes (G3663) — of like passions (Jas 5:17). The cache tags the phrase, not a free-standing English like. This page does not invent a second number.

Usage

"Be not ye therefore like unto them (Matt 6:8) — prayer is not copied from the heathen."

"Idolatry makes God like corruptible man (Rom 1:23); the gospel makes the Son like unto his brethren in true flesh (Heb 2:17)."

"Elijah had like passions (Jas 5:17); the saints will be like him when He appears (1 John 3:2)."
